title: Structured Logging, Event Taxonomy, and Redaction Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies structured logging, event taxonomy, and redaction?
options: Emit stable bounded events through a typed facade and redact sensitive data before it reaches any backend.
questions.answer: Emit stable bounded events through a typed facade and redact sensitive data before it reaches any backend.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Removing sensitive fields from the dashboard after ingestion prevents the original disclosure.
questions.explanation: Logging an entire exception request object can silently include tokens, user content, URLs, and high-cardinality values even when the top-level message looks harmless.

questions.prompt: Why should correlation values be bounded and non-identifying?
questions.answer: They connect related operations without exposing identity or creating unbounded grouping cardinality.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
